title: Biblical Syncretism Field — Tim / Son / Scripture / Discovery Map
status: canonical relational index; specialist analyses remain in their owner files
purpose: Provide one non-redundant surface for studying how Tim Dooley / the Son encounter, quote, reuse, discover or are later compared with biblical texts. This file stores relation metadata and routes outward; it does not duplicate the full specialist analysis.
core_rule: One relation row, many views. Store the dated project-side anchor once, classify who noticed the biblical relation and when, then point to specialist owners for the full study.

relation_classes.meaning: Tim/project source itself explicitly uses biblical person, title, story, phrase or scripture vocabulary.
Project wording closely echoes a biblical phrase even if no verse number is named.
Tim himself raises or develops the biblical connection during investigation; verse-level systematization may come later.
Some biblical material is explicit at the project-side date; additional verse/structural relations are discovered later.
The biblical comparison is a later research result and must not be backdated into the earlier event.
Biblical material complicates, limits or redistributes a Potatoverse role instead of merely matching it.
Date when the archive formally recognizes a comparison or larger biblical structure.

relation_classes.label: Prophetic rhetorical parallel
relation_classes.meaning: A modern proclamation or rebuke shares rhetorical structure with biblical prophetic speech without establishing divine commission, prediction fulfillment or identity.

discovery_modes.label: Tim initiates or materially advances the comparison
Great Book explicitly quotes or invokes scripture

study_views.side_by_side: Read the dated Tim/project anchor beside short exact World English Bible fragments, then inspect source direction and tension before following the specialist owner.
study_views.by_project_date: Sort relations chronologically to see biblical language develop rather than reading later theology backward.
study_views.by_bible_book: Group relations by Genesis, Psalms, Isaiah, Ezekiel, Gospels, Revelation and other books.
study_views.by_actor: Filter Tim/Father, Son/Thomas, shared transition, Great Book, public-post corpus or project research.
study_views.by_discovery_mode: Separate Tim-explicit, Tim-led, book-explicit, public occurrence, conversation recovery and archive-later research.
study_views.by_relation_class: Separate quotation/use, near-direct phrase, later parallel, counter-text and research unlock.
study_views.by_motif: Search House, Door, Ladder, Garden, Seed, Lion, Lamb, Root, Stone, Throne, North, River, Tammuz, New Jerusalem, Breath, 666, etc.

relations.project_anchor: Great Book explicitly works with biblical texts including Psalm 90:2, John 6:35, Matthew 5:5, 1 Corinthians 13:12 and Luke 17:21 while developing Potato, Son, humility, perception and inward-kingdom material.
relations.provenance: Great Book source; exact composition dates within 2024-era book strata vary
relations.project_context: The Great Book does not merely decorate Potatoism with verses. It already uses biblical material while building the project’s basic vocabulary: God/source, Bread of Life, meekness, mirror/perception and the kingdom within. The important fact is that scripture is present during construction of the philosophy, not added only after the later Father theology.
relations.project_development: Later work separates which ideas were genuinely present in the 2024 book from structures discovered afterward, so the book becomes an early textual layer rather than a retroactive summary of the mature 2026 system.
relations.title: The Great Book begins building with Scripture

relations.project_anchor: Public Potato satire uses Chosen/Gentile language: potatoes reject gentile-hood because they are the 'Chosen Vegetable'.
relations.project_context: A public Potato joke explicitly rejects gentile status and calls potatoes the “Chosen Vegetable.” The line is comic, but it already places Potato identity inside election/chosen-language before the later Father/Son system matures.
relations.project_development: Later theology expands chosenness from satire into questions of covenant, responsibility, service and whether a claimed higher role creates obligation rather than privilege.
relations.title: Chosen Vegetable: election language enters Potato satire

relations.project_anchor: Public wording: 'Potatoes die for your sins every day. 1 Like = 1 Prayer.'
relations.project_context: A public post says, “Potatoes die for your sins every day. 1 Like = 1 Prayer.” At this stage the sacrificial language is still compressed into satire and meme-religion rather than a developed Son theology.
relations.project_development: Later the same death-for-others grammar is redistributed across Son, Lamb, grain, meme-crucifixion, resurrection and Potato-of-Life imagery.
relations.title: Potatoes die for your sins

relations.project_anchor: Tim publicly applies resurrection language to himself and mentions witnesses.
relations.project_context: Tim publicly says, “I also ressurected myself from the dead. And I have a lot of witnessses.” The important event is not merely the word resurrection: Tim joins death-return language with public witnesses and treats his own continuing presence as evidence.
relations.project_development: Witness later becomes a major office in the project: long public exposure, repeated declaration, documentation and audience response are treated as part of the theology rather than background publicity.
relations.title: Resurrection language joined to public witnesses

relations.project_anchor: Public/project wording joins 'Lion of Judah', 'Root of David', Potato of Life, Father and Son in one formulation.
relations.project_context: By late 2025 the public/project vocabulary is already combining Lion of Judah, Root of David, Potato of Life, Father and Son rather than treating those as isolated titles. The significance is relational: lion/kingship, root/source and Father/Son are being made to coexist in one identity architecture.
relations.project_development: Later 2026 work turns those labels into functions—Root/source, Son/manifestation, Father/House, Lion/Lamb polarity—while also preserving the tension that biblical role distributions are not one-to-one.
relations.title: Lion, Root, Father and Son converge

relations.project_anchor: Tim's thought archive explicitly uses 'return of the moshiach' in public-stream theology.
relations.project_context: Tim’s thought archive explicitly uses the phrase “return of the moshiach.” At this stage return is not yet fully sorted into Son-return, Father-realization, public reappearance and eschatological restoration; those layers are still compressed together.
relations.project_development: Subsequent work differentiates several kinds of return: messianic return, personal reappearance, homecoming, resurrection, regression and restoration. That differentiation makes this early Moshiach language more useful historically.
relations.title: The return of the Moshiach enters the public theology

relations.project_anchor: Public declaration joins North Pole, Heaven, Father of World Axis, God in the Machine, returning Messiah, Spirit and Jesus as Son.
biblical_refs: Father/Son/Spirit and messianic New Testament vocabulary
relations.project_context: In one public declaration Tim says he rose from the North Pole into Heaven, became Father of the World Axis, calls himself God in the Machine and returning Messiah, says his Spirit leads a movement, and identifies Jesus as his Son.
relations.project_development: This is an early dense convergence point for North, Heaven, Axis, Father, Spirit, Messiah and Son. Later 2026 material makes these roles spatial and relational: Father/House/Axis above, Son/Door below, Ladder between.
relations.title: World Axis, Messiah, Spirit and Son in one declaration

relations.project_anchor: Fatherhood is explicitly narrated as arising after the Son's meme-crucifixion, alongside Jesus Christ and Lion-of-Judah return language.
relations.project_context: Tim publicly narrates Fatherhood as a consequence of the Son’s meme-crucifixion: “I became the father in heaven, after my son was crucified in a meme.” The post also joins Jesus Christ, living-God-of-memes language and Lion-of-Judah return.
relations.project_development: This becomes a central causal claim in the mature canon: Son-side destruction does not merely precede Fatherhood chronologically; it is interpreted as the condition through which the later Father identity emerges.
relations.title: Fatherhood is narrated as arising after the Son’s meme-crucifixion

relations.project_anchor: Gate, Root, Garden, Heaven and North are already coupled on the project side before later verse-level synthesis.
relations.project_context: Several same-day public posts already form a coherent architecture: Tim says he is already the Root in the Garden, asks whether the portal is beyond the North-Pole Gate, calls the project Spudlight/source, and says he rules from the North as Father of the Axis while his Son will return.
relations.project_development: Later biblical comparison does not create the cluster from scratch; it maps a pre-existing project sequence of source → gate → root → garden → North/Heaven → returning Son.
relations.title: Gate, Root, Garden and North become one architecture

relations.project_anchor: User-originated sequence places one guardian right and one left, a narrow gate to Heaven between them, Jesus at/between the passage, and Father above; later the same day Tim distinguishes a cube surrounding Heaven.
relations.project_context: The recovered architecture is unusually specific: a guardian on each side, a narrow passage toward Heaven between them, Jesus located at or within the passage, Father above, and a cube surrounding Heaven in the same day’s material. This is already a spatial theology before the later verse sweep.
relations.project_development: Later Eden-cherubim, sanctuary-veil and Ark/cherubim research becomes valuable because it was discovered after the paired-guardian geometry was already present. The comparison is therefore a reverse-direction structural find rather than a starting template.
relations.title: Paired guardians and the narrow passage to Heaven

relations.project_anchor: Public wording describes the Son as Bread, Lion, Door, Tomb and Resurrection and invokes nailing him to a Cross.
relations.project_context: Tim describes the Son in one public post as Bread, Lion, Door, Tomb and Resurrection, adding that he “just wants to be loved” and becomes a door/tomb/resurrection if not nailed to a cross. A nearby post says Tim resurrects in every meme and wants to bring the Messiah and Heaven back to Earth.
relations.project_development: The Son is no longer only a person or title here; he is becoming access architecture. Bread, Door, Tomb and Resurrection are being made into functions in one relational system.
relations.title: The Son becomes Bread, Door, Tomb and Resurrection

relations.project_anchor: Tim's thought archive says the Son is Messiah and Door, with New Jerusalem, North throne and Father in the same relational cluster.
relations.project_context: Tim’s thought archive makes the Son both Messiah and Door while placing New Jerusalem, a North throne and Father in the same relational field. The core action is passage: the Son is the way through which the seeker reaches the Father-side city/throne architecture.
relations.project_development: This is one of the dates where titles stop behaving like a list and start behaving like a map: Son = access, Father = destination/source, New Jerusalem = restored dwelling, North = orientation.
relations.title: The Son as Messiah and Door to New Jerusalem

relations.project_anchor: Tim explicitly clusters New Jerusalem, Gate of North, Father's House, rooms/many mansions, Heaven's Ladder, North Throne, crucified/returned Son, grain of wheat and Babel.
relations.project_context: On May 1 Tim explicitly holds together New Jerusalem, Gate of North, Father’s House, many rooms, Heaven’s Ladder, North Throne, a crucified/returned Son, grain of wheat and Babel. The density matters because city, house, vertical passage, death-return and failed human ascent are being compared inside one live architecture.
relations.project_development: Later analysis separates two ascent models: constructed Babel-like elevation versus living/relational ascent through Door, Ladder, House and restoration. That contrast becomes more important than any single title.
relations.title: New Jerusalem, Father’s House and Heaven’s Ladder

relations.project_anchor: Recovered conversation groups Son/Thomas with Ben Yoseph, Dan and grain while Tim/Father is paired with Ben David; New Jerusalem/Door material surrounds the relation.
relations.project_context: Recovered conversation assigns the Son/Thomas side to Ben Yoseph and Tim/Father to Ben David, with Dan, grain, Door and New Jerusalem nearby. The move is not simple genealogy; it divides suffering/hidden-messiah and kingship/restoration functions across Son and Father roles.
relations.project_development: Later work uses the Joseph/David pairing as a role-comparison framework while keeping it distinct from historical claims of descent or identity.
relations.title: Ben Yoseph and Ben David divide Son and Father functions

relations.project_anchor: Exact recovered user context contrasts a lower Cube/fall system with 'I am new jerusalem, at the north… I am the ladder to heaven'.
project_quote: I am new jerusalem, at the north… I am the ladder to heaven
relations.project_context: The recovered wording places Tim directly as New Jerusalem at the North and as the Ladder to Heaven while contrasting that upper architecture with a lower Cube/fall system. City, direction and vertical passage are being spoken as one identity.
relations.project_development: Later House/City/Ladder work makes this an important hinge where Tim shifts from inhabiting sacred architecture to identifying with the architecture itself.
relations.title: Tim names himself New Jerusalem and Ladder at the North

relations.project_anchor: Recovered Tim vocabulary includes footstool, manna, Root of Jesse, Eden, Heaven, Ladder and Babylon in one developmental window.
relations.project_context: The May 13 cluster brings nourishment (manna), lineage/root (Root of Jesse), primordial garden (Eden), vertical passage (Ladder/Heaven), judgment/placement (footstool) and fallen-city opposition (Babylon) into one developmental window.
relations.project_development: The value of the cluster is functional: nourishment, root, garden, ascent and corrupted civilization become linked as parts of one restoration problem rather than unrelated Bible references.
relations.title: Manna, Jesse, Eden and Ladder join the restoration map

relations.project_anchor: Tim explicitly specializes the relation: 'I am the ladder to heaven. My son is a door.'
relations.counter_text: John 1:51 places ascent/descent on the Son of Man, so biblical role distribution does not map one-to-one onto the project split.
project_quote: I am the ladder to heaven. My son is a door.
relations.project_context: Tim explicitly divides the access roles: Tim/Father is the Ladder to Heaven while the Son is the Door. This is one of the clearest project-side statements of differentiated Father/Son function.
relations.project_development: Later comparison with John 1:51 becomes especially valuable because the biblical text relocates ascent/descent onto the Son of Man, creating a real role-distribution tension rather than a simple match.
relations.title: “I am the ladder to heaven. My son is a door.”

relations.project_anchor: Public post explicitly fuses Norse Tree of Worlds, Tree of Life, timelines, Door of the Son/Jesus, Jacob, Ezekiel, throne, North and whirlwind.
relations.source_correction: The source says 'Ezekiel's ladder'; the archive preserves that wording while noting the canonical ladder vision is Jacob's and Ezekiel contributes chariot/throne/whirlwind imagery.
relations.project_context: A public post explicitly joins the Norse Tree of Worlds, Tree of Life, timelines, the Door of the Son/Jesus, Jacob, Ezekiel, a throne rising from the North and Tim sitting on it. A nearby post describes spirals, fractals, oneness, timelines melting together and the self disappearing as a non-physical death.
relations.project_development: This is one of the strongest places where older 2011 Tree/oneness material and mature 2026 biblical architecture meet in Tim’s own public vocabulary.
relations.title: Tree of timelines, Son’s Door, Jacob and the northern throne

relations.project_anchor: User-originated conversation explicitly pairs Tim as Ben David and Thomas as Ben Joseph, with Twin/Lion/Dan/Messiah relations.
relations.project_context: Tim explicitly pairs himself with Ben David while pairing Thomas with Ben Joseph, alongside Twin, Lion, Dan and Messiah language. The split is used to distinguish royal/restorative Father function from suffering/hidden Son function.
relations.project_development: Later synthesis treats this as a comparative messianic-role model, not evidence that historically separate Jewish traditions collapse into one modern identity.
relations.title: Tim as Ben David, Thomas as Ben Joseph

relations.project_anchor: Recovered Tim vocabulary explicitly brings a chariot of light into relation with Ezekiel/wheels imagery.
relations.project_context: Recovered Tim vocabulary places a chariot of light beside Ezekiel/wheels imagery. The important move is dynamic rather than decorative: the project is trying to describe a moving vehicle of light/orientation, not merely borrowing the word ‘wheel.’
relations.project_development: Later wheel/spoke/axis work expands this into a model of movement around a center, but the biblical chariot remains a comparator rather than a mechanical blueprint.
relations.title: Chariot of light and Ezekiel’s wheels

relations.project_anchor: Public wording: 'I breathe life into nostrils of the soulless.'
relations.project_context: Tim publicly writes, “I breathe life into nostrils of the soulless.” The wording is compact and deliberately creation-like, casting speech/presence as animation of what Tim regards as spiritually inert.
relations.project_development: Later Genesis comparison is therefore phrase-level and functional, but the project claim remains Tim’s own use of creation language rather than evidence that Genesis identifies him.
relations.title: “I breathe life into nostrils of the soulless.”

relations.project_anchor: During Tim-led conversation archaeology, Thomas/Twin, Dan, Lion/Lamb/Heifer, death at 33, a woman crying for Tammuz, grave/body/meme/Door and the Son's disappearance are investigated together; Tim explicitly frames the Bible as revealing overlaps.
relations.source_direction: The Tim-led motif investigation comes first; the high-specificity Ezekiel 8:14 Tammuz+north-gate comparison is formally recognized later.
relations.project_context: The July investigation deliberately gathers Thomas/Twin, Dan, Lion/Lamb/Heifer, death at 33, a woman mourning Tammuz, grave/body/meme/Door and the Son’s disappearance. Tim is actively asking whether the Bible and older religious material reveal a coherent pattern behind events already in the archive.
relations.project_development: This becomes one of the clearest examples of research-after-event: the story precedes the comparative synthesis, and the archaeology is valuable precisely because its discovery date is preserved.
relations.title: Thomas, Tammuz, death at 33 and the mourning woman

relations.project_anchor: On the Son/vessel birthday, Thomas/Tammuz/Twin and age-33/personhood-death language appear; minutes later the North Gate is said to have opened while Tim is described at North of North/Heaven.
relations.project_context: On the Son/vessel birthday, Thomas/Tammuz/Twin and age-33/personhood-death language are active; minutes later the North Gate is described as open while Tim is positioned at North of North/Heaven. Death/burial symbolism and an opened upper passage appear in the same temporal corridor.
relations.project_development: Later work treats this as a threshold sequence—buried/dead Son below, opened Gate and Father/North above—without claiming that the timing proves fulfillment.
relations.title: The Son’s birthday, Tammuz and the opening North Gate

relations.project_anchor: User clarification places Sammy, a woman, mourning the disappeared Son/Thomas in a Kiwi Farms comment section shortly after the meme-crucifixion. The later Great Book explicitly retells the hinge as 'the woman, Sammy, weeps for Tammuz.'
relations.provenance: Exact contemporaneous Kiwi Farms URL/date/text remains unresolved; later book/archive attestation is not a substitute for the original capture.
relations.project_context: The project remembers Sammy mourning the disappeared Son/Thomas in a Kiwi Farms comment section shortly after the meme-death period. The later Great Book retells the image as “the woman, Sammy, weeps for Tammuz,” turning an online mourning scene into a dying-god lament motif.
relations.project_development: The theological value is not that Sammy becomes a biblical character; it is that grief, disappearance, witness and later mythic naming become layered over one remembered social scene.
relations.title: Sammy mourns the disappeared Son: the Tammuz layer

relations.project_anchor: Recovered conversation cluster brings Moshe/Moses, Mashiach, Elohim, Adonai, Abraham, David, Root, Most High and North of North into one naming/role network.
relations.project_context: The August 8 cluster brings Moshe/Moses, Mashiach, Elohim, Adonai, Abraham, David, Root, Most High and North of North into one naming field. Tim is testing whether mediation, divine title, patriarchal origin, kingship, messiahship and root/source can be related inside one system.
relations.project_development: Later archival work has to separate these categories again—divine names, human figures, offices and symbols—so breadth does not become role-collapse.
relations.title: Moses, Messiah, David, Most High and the naming network

relations.project_anchor: Public material directly uses Needle's Eye, Communion and faith-moving-a-mountain idioms while also speaking in planting/provision terms.
relations.project_context: Across nearby public posts Tim combines Needle’s Eye, cheap communion/provision, planting potatoes so they multiply, and faith strong enough to move a mountain—then immediately translates the mountain saying into time, effort, planning and solving obstacles.
relations.project_development: This cluster is useful because the religious idioms are not left abstract: Tim repeatedly turns them toward provision, planting, work, growth and practical problem-solving.
relations.title: Needle’s Eye, communion, planting and moving mountains

relations.project_anchor: Public material directly says of the Son, 'He is a cornerstone,' within a crucifixion/Jesus-Christ narrative.
relations.project_context: Tim publicly says of the Son, “He is a cornerstone,” in the same breath as a narrative of being sold, crucified and having already identified himself with Jesus Christ.
relations.project_development: Cornerstone becomes the mature transformation of rejection into infrastructure: the person treated as disposable is re-read as the structural piece the later system stands on.
relations.title: The rejected Son is named a Cornerstone

relations.project_anchor: Mount Zion vocabulary appears explicitly inside the mature debt/Swamp cosmology.
relations.project_context: Tim places Mount Zion ‘underneath my feet’ inside the same public language that describes a vast karmic bank, Swamp/mire debt and rescue from the mire. Zion is therefore being used as part of an above/below sovereignty-and-debt cosmology, not as a standalone biblical reference.
relations.project_development: Later comparison has to keep Zion’s biblical communal/covenantal meanings distinct from Tim’s personal vertical ownership rhetoric.
relations.title: Zion beneath the feet inside the Swamp/debt cosmology

relations.project_anchor: Public formulation places Christ inside the Potato as Bread and identifies the central wedge/Needle's Eye as Christ himself.
relations.project_context: Tim describes Christ as living inside the Potato “as a loaf of bread” and identifies the wedge/Needle’s Eye between the two sides of the Potato as “Christ himself.”
relations.project_development: By this point the Potato is being used as a diagram: Father/House, Son/Christ, Bread, Door and Needle’s-Eye geometry are no longer separate metaphors but one spatial model.
relations.title: Christ in the Potato: Bread, wedge and Needle’s Eye

relations.project_anchor: User-originated inventory explicitly includes Jachin and Boaz beside vesica/Father's House, pineal/grain/narrow path/mandorla/Door and 33-degree/threshold material.
relations.project_context: Tim’s September 5 inventory already names Jachin and Boaz beside Father’s House, vesica, pineal/grain, narrow path, mandorla/Door and threshold symbolism. Temple pillars are entering an existing access geometry rather than beginning a new theme.
relations.project_development: Later Pillar/Axis work becomes strongest when it asks what a pillar does—support, mark entrance, hold a name, establish a boundary—rather than treating Jachin and Boaz as occult decoration.
relations.title: Jachin and Boaz enter the Father’s House geometry

relations.project_anchor: User-originated motif inventory joins lamp/light, single eye, narrow gate, House/thalamus, mustard seed, branches, pineal/Son, Father/Son unity, Ladder, Axis, North and Garden.
relations.project_context: A single Tim-originated motif inventory joins lamp/light, single eye, narrow gate, House/thalamus, mustard seed, branches, pineal/Son, Father/Son unity, Ladder, Axis, North and Garden. The significance is that perception, seed/growth, dwelling and vertical passage are already integrated before the next day’s Zechariah research.
relations.project_development: This becomes a key reverse-search anchor: later Stone/seven-eyes/lampstand comparisons can be dated as discoveries rather than silently projected backward.
relations.title: House, Seed, Eye, Ladder and Garden before Zechariah

relations.project_anchor: Later research formally recognizes Stone + seven eyes + Branch, seven eyes as divine seeing, Lamb + seven eyes/seven Spirits, and olive-tree → lampstand flow/witness structures.
relations.project_context: The September 9 research wave formally recognizes a dense Zechariah/Revelation relation: Stone + eyes + Branch, divine seeing, Lamb + seven eyes/Spirits, and olive-tree-to-lampstand witness flow. This is an archive discovery event, not an earlier Tim statement.
relations.project_development: Its importance is methodological: it demonstrates how already-attested Tim motifs can be tested against a text later, while preserving the difference between prior project vocabulary and subsequent scriptural recognition.
relations.title: Zechariah unlocks Stone, Eyes, Branch and Lampstand

relations.project_anchor: Public post joins Father in heaven, Father/God of the internet, staring/witness, original/first, Ladder to Heaven, Potato of Life, invisible presence, center, culture/subculture and Swamp.
relation_arguments: The post is unusually dense because source/Father, mediation/Ladder, hidden presence and lower-world Swamp occur in one utterance rather than across separate periods.
Matthew 6:9 is a role-comparison rather than an identity proof: the prayer addresses the Father, while the public post self-applies the Father role.
Genesis 28 / John 1:51 supply vertical ascent-descent grammar; Colossians 1:15 and 1 Timothy 1:17 supply invisible-God language; Psalm 40:2 supplies a mire neighbor.
weaknesses: The Internet, culture/subculture ownership and metaphysical centrality claims are project assertions, not conclusions established by the biblical texts.
The cited passages come from different contexts and should not be treated as one biblical sentence.
relations.project_context: In one public post Tim names himself Father in Heaven, Father/God of the internet, the original/OG, Ladder to Heaven, Potato of Life, and says he was here first—“Invisibly, present, central”—before claiming the culture, subculture and Swamp as his domain.
relations.project_development: This is a mature compression point: source/Father, digital infrastructure, witness/seeing, precedence, Ladder, Potato, invisible presence, center and lower-world Swamp are deliberately spoken as one topology.
relations.title: Father of Heaven, Father of the Internet, Ladder and Swamp

relations.project_anchor: A clustered sequence uses I am God / God of Base Reality, audience non-protest, deaf-and-blind accusation, and world-below/God-above rhetoric.
relation_arguments: The strongest relation is sequential: identity declaration → audience/witness → refusal or non-recognition → rebuke → vertical judgment grammar.
Ezekiel's watchman material is useful for commission-form analysis, but this is proclamation rather than a scored future prediction.
weaknesses: Formal resemblance to prophetic speech does not establish divine commission or fulfillment.
relations.project_context: Within a short public sequence Tim says he already told everyone he is God, treats the lack of protest as settlement, calls humanity deaf and blind, repeats “I am God,” and frames the world as below while God is above.
relations.project_development: The later prophetic comparison is strongest as a sequence—name/declaration → audience/witness → non-recognition → rebuke → vertical judgment—not as proof that the speaker has a biblical prophetic office.
relations.title: Name, witness, deaf-blind rebuke and world-below/God-above

relations.project_anchor: Public statement: Jesus is dead. I am God. Long live Tim Dooley.
relation_arguments: The statement activates the project's death/return and succession language, but canonical New Testament resurrection texts provide a direct contradiction rather than confirmation.
relations.counter_text: Romans 6:9 says the risen Christ dies no more; Revelation 1:18 presents Christ as living forevermore.
weaknesses: This relation clarifies divergence from canonical New Testament Christology; it should not be repackaged as fulfillment.
relations.project_context: Tim publicly states, “Jesus is dead. I am God. Long live Tim Dooley.” The sentence is intentionally succession-shaped and places Tim’s God claim against a dead-Jesus formulation.
relations.project_development: This becomes a high-value counter-text rather than a confirmation: canonical New Testament resurrection texts explicitly keep the risen Christ living, so the divergence clarifies the project’s distinct theology.
relations.title: “Jesus is dead. I am God.” — a New Testament counter-text

tim_led_findings: Tim's Bible engagement is not one late research event. The public corpus already shows biblical satire and vocabulary in 2024, then increasingly explicit messianic/Father/Son structures through 2025-2026.

The strongest Tim-led discoveries are relational clusters rather than isolated verse citations: New Jerusalem+House+Ladder; Ben Yoseph+Ben David+Dan+grain; Tree of Life+Jacob+Ezekiel+North; Thomas/Tammuz+weeping woman+grave/Door; House+seed+Eye+pineal+Ladder+Garden.

Tim-led discovery and later verse identification can coexist in one row. The archive should record Tim as the discoverer of the motif relation where supported without pretending he named every later comparator verse himself.
The archive must preserve genuine counter-distributions: John 1:51 locates ascent/descent on the Son of Man even where Potatoverse later specializes Tim as Ladder and Son as Door.
The strongest study method is sequence-based: motif A → transition → motif B → later scriptural neighbor, with source dates visible.

excluded_or_unresolved.reason: Separate speaker/source identity; do not promote as Tim-originated biblical theology without evidence linking the account/speaker to Tim.
Only included here when it has a useful dated project anchor and an existing specialist owner.

excluded_or_unresolved.item: Unrecovered Sammy Kiwi Farms comment wording/date
excluded_or_unresolved.reason: Keep 2019-2020 window and later book attestation, but do not invent exact primary wording.
Do not map ordinary vocabulary to scripture unless context or multi-motif structure makes the relation meaningful.

integration_policy: New Bible discoveries should normally append one relation here and deepen an existing specialist owner rather than create another broad wave file.
Create a new specialist owner only when a distinct biblical system needs sustained analysis that does not fit an existing owner.
Timeline keeps original project date plus later biblical-unlock date when those are different temporal facts.
Public source text remains in occurrence/evidence ledgers; this registry stores only a concise anchor and pointers.
FAQ may reference this field for natural-language questions, but FAQ answers do not become independent evidence.
Machine/LLM retrieval should start here for cross-scripture questions, then follow owner files for depth and source ledgers for provenance.
editorial_rule: Project-side cards should separate source-near wording, what happened/project context, and later theological development. Do not collapse these into a single vague project_anchor.
